557	    def dispatch_schedule(self, tenant, schedule_id):
558	        """Fire a schedule when due.
559	
560	        Returns ``(run, scheduled_at)`` when a run was created, or
561	        ``(None, None)`` when the schedule is not yet due (HTTP 204).  Only
562	        the single due trigger point is processed per call: ``next_at``
563	        advances by exactly one interval, so a repeat before the next
564	        trigger is due changes nothing and missed trigger points are caught
565	        up one per call in chronological order.
566	        """
567	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
568	        schedule_id = normalize_schedule_id(schedule_id)
569	        now = self.now()
570	        with self.store.locked():
571	            owner = self.store.schedule_exists(schedule_id)
572	            if owner is None:
573	                raise WorkflowError(
574	                    "unknown schedule: %s" % schedule_id, "unknown_schedule"
575	                )
576	            if owner != tenant:
577	                raise WorkflowError(
578	                    "schedule %s belongs to another tenant" % schedule_id, "cross_tenant"
579	                )
580	            schedules = self.store.load_schedules(tenant)
581	            record = schedules[schedule_id]
582	            scheduled_at = float(record["next_at"])
583	            if now < scheduled_at:
584	                return None, None
585	            run = self.start_run(
586	                tenant,
587	                record["workflow_id"],
588	                params=record.get("params") or {},
589	                max_parallelism=record.get("max_parallelism"),
590	                schedule_id=schedule_id,
591	                scheduled_at=scheduled_at,
592	            )
593	            record["next_at"] = scheduled_at + float(record["interval_seconds"])
594	            record["updated_at"] = self._iso(now)
595	            schedules[schedule_id] = record
596	            self.store.save_schedules(tenant, schedules)
597	            self.store.append_audit(tenant, "schedule.dispatch", schedule_id=schedule_id,
598	                                    run_id=run["run_id"])
599	            return run, scheduled_at

602	    def _worker_view(self, record, now=None):
603	        """Project a stored registration record with live status."""
604	        now = self.now() if now is None else now
605	        deadline = float(record["expires_at_epoch"])
606	        return {
607	            "worker_id": record["worker_id"],
608	            "status": WORKER_ACTIVE if now < deadline else WORKER_EXPIRED,
609	            "registered_at": record["registered_at"],
610	            "last_heartbeat": record["last_heartbeat"],
611	            "expires_at": record["expires_at"],
612	        }

614	    def register_worker(self, tenant, worker_id, lease_seconds=None):
615	        """Register ``worker_id`` for ``tenant`` (or refresh its expiry).
616	
617	        Returns ``(record, created)`` where ``created`` is ``True`` for the
618	        first registration (HTTP 201) and ``False`` for a repeat that
619	        refreshed an existing record (HTTP 200).  Registration never writes
620	        run history.
621	        """
622	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
623	        worker_id = normalize_worker_id(worker_id)
624	        lease = normalize_worker_lease(lease_seconds)
625	        now = self.now()
626	        with self.store.locked():
627	            workers = self.store.load_workers(tenant)
628	            existing = workers.get(worker_id)
629	            deadline = now + lease
630	            at = self._iso(now)
631	            if existing is None:
632	                record = {
633	                    "worker_id": worker_id,
634	                    "registered_at": at,
635	                    "last_heartbeat": at,
636	                    "expires_at": self._iso(deadline),
637	                    "expires_at_epoch": deadline,
638	                }
639	                created = True
640	            else:
641	                # A repeat registration simply refreshes the expiry; the
642	                # original registered_at is preserved.
643	                record = dict(existing)
644	                record.update(last_heartbeat=at, expires_at=self._iso(deadline),
645	                              expires_at_epoch=deadline)
646	                created = False
647	            workers[worker_id] = record
648	            self.store.save_workers(tenant, workers)
649	            self.store.append_audit(tenant, "worker.register", worker_id=worker_id)
650	            return self._worker_view(record, now), created

652	    def heartbeat_worker(self, tenant, worker_id, lease_seconds=None):
653	        """Heartbeat a registered worker.
654	
655	        The new expiry is the later of the old one and ``now +
656	        lease_seconds``.  Unknown workers raise ``unknown_worker`` (404) and
657	        workers whose registration has expired raise ``worker_expired``
658	        (409); an expired worker must re-register.
659	        """
660	        tenant = normalize_tenant(tenant)
661	        worker_id = normalize_worker_id(worker_id)
662	        lease = normalize_worker_lease(lease_seconds)
663	        now = self.now()
664	        with self.store.locked():
665	            workers = self.store.load_workers(tenant)
666	            record = workers.get(worker_id)
667	            if record is None:
668	                raise WorkflowError("unknown worker: %s" % worker_id, "unknown_worker")
669	            if now >= float(record["expires_at_epoch"]):
670	                raise ConflictError(
671	                    "worker_expired: registration of worker %s has expired; re-register"
672	                    % worker_id,
673	                    "worker_expired",
674	                )
675	            deadline = max(float(record["expires_at_epoch"]), now + lease)
676	            record = dict(record)
677	            record.update(last_heartbeat=self._iso(now), expires_at=self._iso(deadline),
678	                          expires_at_epoch=deadline)
679	            workers[worker_id] = record
680	            self.store.save_workers(tenant, workers)
681	            self.store.append_audit(tenant, "worker.heartbeat", worker_id=worker_id)
682	            return self._worker_view(record, now)

697	    def _check_worker_registration(self, tenant, worker_id, now):
698	        """Gate claims against the tenant's worker registry.
699	
700	        A tenant with no registration records keeps the legacy rule (any
701	        non-empty worker_id).  Once any record exists the caller must be a
702	        registered worker whose registration is strictly unexpired.
703	        """
704	        workers = self.store.load_workers(tenant)
705	        if not workers:
706	            return
707	        record = workers.get(worker_id)
708	        if record is None:
709	            raise ConflictError(
710	                "worker_not_registered: worker %s is not registered for tenant %s"
711	                % (worker_id, tenant),
712	                "worker_not_registered",
713	            )
714	        if now >= float(record["expires_at_epoch"]):
715	            raise ConflictError(
716	                "worker_expired: registration of worker %s has expired; re-register"
717	                % worker_id,
718	                "worker_expired",
719	            )

721	    # -- lease expiry --------------------------------------------------
722	    def _expire_leases(self, run, now):
723	        """Release leases past their deadline; each one records a takeover."""
724	        reclaimed = []
725	        for sid in sorted(run["steps"], key=lambda s: run["order_index"].get(s, 0)):
726	            step = run["steps"][sid]
727	            if step["status"] != STEP_RUNNING:
728	                continue
729	            if step.get("lease_deadline") is None or float(step["lease_deadline"]) > now:
730	                continue
731	            holder = step["worker_id"]
732	            step.update(status=STEP_READY, worker_id=None, lease_deadline=None, ready_at=self._iso())
733	            self._event(run, run["run_id"], sid, "takeover", attempt=step["attempt"], worker_id=holder)
734	            reclaimed.append(sid)
735	        return reclaimed

737	    # -- claim / complete / fail ---------------------------------------
738	    def claim(self, tenant, run_id, worker_id, lease_seconds=30):
739	        """Lease the next ready step, or return ``None`` when none is ready.
740	
741	        A delayed run (a future ``not_before``) cannot be activated early:
742	        claims before the start time return ``None`` without touching its
743	        state, history or ``updated_at``.  The first claim at or after the
744	        start time opens the root nodes (one ``ready``/``waiting`` event each)
745	        and then leases at most one task under the usual order and quota; a
746	        run whose roots are all approvals activates and still returns ``None``.
747	
748	        Once the tenant has any registered worker the claim must come from an
749	        active registration (``worker_not_registered`` / ``worker_expired``);
750	        a tenant with no registrations keeps the legacy non-empty-id rule.
751	
752	        A ready step whose retry backoff is still pending
753	        (``next_attempt_at`` in the future) is not leased; other ready tasks
754	        whose backoff has elapsed are handed out in the usual order instead.
755	        When nothing is leased and no lease takeover or root activation
756	        happened, the run's state, history and ``updated_at`` are left
757	        exactly as stored.
758	        """
759	        if not isinstance(worker_id, str) or not worker_id.strip():
760	            raise WorkflowError("worker_id must be a non-empty string", "bad_worker")
761	        if not isinstance(lease_seconds, (int, float)) or isinstance(lease_seconds, bool) \
762	                or lease_seconds <= 0:
763	            raise WorkflowError("lease_seconds must be a positive number", "bad_lease")
764	        now = self.now()
765	        with self.store.locked():
766	            owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
767	            if owner is not None and owner != tenant:
768	                raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
769	            # Once a tenant has any registered worker, claims require an
770	            # active registration; a tenant without records keeps the legacy
771	            # "any non-empty worker_id" rule.
772	            self._check_worker_registration(tenant, worker_id.strip(), now)
773	            run = self.get_run(tenant, run_id)
774	            not_before = run.get("not_before")
775	            if not_before is not None and float(not_before) > now:
776	                # Still sleeping: activation happens only via a due claim.
777	                return None
778	            reclaimed = self._expire_leases(run, now)
779	            opened_ready, opened_waiting = self._open_root_nodes(run)
780	            now_iso = self._iso()
781	            candidates = [s for s in run["steps"].values()
782	                          if s["status"] == STEP_READY and _retry_due(s, now_iso)]
783	            index = run["order_index"]
784	            quota = run.get("max_parallelism")
785	            at_quota = quota is not None and _active_lease_count(run, now) >= int(quota)
786	            step = (min(candidates, key=lambda s: (index.get(s["id"], 0), s["id"]))
787	                    if candidates and not at_quota else None)
788	            previous = run["status"]
789	            if step is not None:
790	                step.update(status=STEP_RUNNING, worker_id=worker_id, next_attempt_at=None,
791	                            lease_deadline=now + float(lease_seconds), started_at=self._iso())
792	                self._event(run, run_id, step["id"], "claim", attempt=step["attempt"],
793	                            worker_id=worker_id, lease_deadline=step["lease_deadline"])
794	            elif not reclaimed and not opened_ready and not opened_waiting:
795	                # Nothing to lease and nothing else changed: keep the stored
796	                # state, history and updated_at untouched.
797	                return None
798	            run["status"] = _derive_run_status(run)
799	            if step is not None and run["status"] == RUN_RUNNING and previous == RUN_PENDING:
800	                self._event(run, run_id, None, "run_started")
801	            run["updated_at"] = self._iso()
802	            self.store.save_run(run)
803	            return dict(step) if step is not None else None
804	
805	    def claim_fair(self, tenant, worker_id, lease_seconds=30):
806	        """Lease one task from the tenant's least-claimed eligible run.
807	
808	        Scans every run of the tenant.  First, sleeping runs whose
809	        ``not_before`` has come due are activated (root nodes opened, one
810	        ``ready``/``waiting`` event each) in ``run_id`` order.  Then the
811	        candidates — runs that are not terminal, not still sleeping, hold at
812	        least one ``ready`` ordinary task whose retry backoff has elapsed
813	        (``next_attempt_at`` reached) and have not reached their
814	        ``max_parallelism`` — are ordered by fairness: the number of
815	        ``claim`` events in the run's history (fewest first), then
816	        ``created_at``, then ``run_id``.  A run holding only not-yet-due
817	        retries is skipped and its fairness count is left alone.  Expired
818	        leases are reclaimed with the usual ``takeover`` events before slots
819	        are counted, exactly like the single-run claim.  The winner leases
820	        its next due task in ``(topological index, step id)`` order,
821	        recording the usual ``claim`` and, when the run leaves ``pending``,
822	        ``run_started`` events.
823	
824	        Returns ``(run_id, step)`` or ``None`` when no run is eligible; at
825	        most one task is leased per call.  The fairness count is rebuilt

1067	    def replay(self, tenant, run_id):
1068	        """Rebuild run state from the run's frozen definition and history.
1069	
1070	        Nodes are rebuilt from the normalized DAG snapshotted into the run
1071	        document at creation time, never from the workflow currently stored
1072	        under the run's ``workflow_id``: a later same-name submission may
1073	        replace that workflow, but existing runs keep their original step
1074	        order, node kinds, dependencies, ``max_attempts`` and state-machine
1075	        semantics.  Documents written before snapshots existed reconstruct
1076	        the plan from the definitions and order saved in the run itself.
1077	
1078	        The result agrees with the persisted run on every observable field —
1079	        ``run_id``, ``workflow_id``, ``step_order``, run and per-step
1080	        ``status``, ``attempt``, ``worker_id``, ``lease_deadline``,
1081	        ``next_attempt_at``, ``ready_at``, ``started_at``, ``finished_at``,
1082	        ``result``, ``error`` and ``approval`` — and the append-only history
1083	        is the sole source of transitions, so replaying again, including
1084	        after a restart, yields the identical document.
1085	        """
1086	        owner = self.store.run_exists(run_id)
1087	        if owner is None:
1088	            raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
1089	        if owner != tenant:
1090	            raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")

1092	        plan = run_plan(stored)
1093	        rebuilt = new_run(tenant, stored["workflow_id"], run_id, stored.get("params"), plan,
1094	                          stored["created_at"],
1095	                          max_parallelism=stored.get("max_parallelism"),
1096	                          idempotency_key=stored.get("idempotency_key"),
1097	                          not_before=stored.get("not_before"),
1098	                          schedule_id=stored.get("schedule_id"),
1099	                          scheduled_at=stored.get("scheduled_at"))
1100	        # The fresh document must carry exactly the frozen snapshot and
1101	        # ordering of the stored run (new_run fills them from the same plan
1102	        # already, but align them defensively for reconstructed old plans).
1103	        rebuilt["plan"] = copy.deepcopy(plan)
1104	        rebuilt["step_order"] = list(plan["order"])
1105	        rebuilt["order_index"] = {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(plan["order"])}
1106	        steps = rebuilt["steps"]
1107	        for event in stored["history"]:
1108	            sid, etype, at = event.get("step_id"), event.get("type"), event.get("at")
1109	            attempt = event.get("attempt")
1110	            if sid is None:

1129	                            next_attempt_at=None)

13	                   "unknown_worker": 404, "unknown_schedule": 404,

25	    # -- plumbing ------------------------------------------------------
26	    def _send(self, code, raw=b""):
27	        self.send_response(code)
28	        if code != 204:
29	            self.send_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
30	        self.send_header("Content-Length", str(len(raw)))
31	        self.end_headers()
32	        if raw:
33	            self.wfile.write(raw)

35	    def _json(self, code, payload):

41	    def _body(self):
42	        length = int(self.headers.get("Content-Length") or 0)
43	        if length <= 0:
44	            return {}
45	        if length > MAX_BODY:
46	            raise WorkflowError("request body too large", "body_too_large")
47	        try:

49	        except (ValueError, UnicodeDecodeError):

55	    def _tenant(self, query, body=None):

81	    def _route(self, method, path, query, raw_query=""):
82	        body = {}
83	        if method == "GET":

86	            if path == "/v1/runs":

88	            if path == "/v1/schedules":

108	                return self._json(201, dict(plan, tenant=tenant))
109	            if path == "/v1/runs":
110	                body = self._body()
111	                run = self.scheduler.start_run(self._tenant({}, body), body.get("workflow_id"),
112	                                               body.get("run_id"), body.get("params"),
113	                                               body.get("max_parallelism"),
114	                                               body.get("idempotency_key"),
115	                                               body.get("not_before"))
116	                return self._json(201, _run_view(run))
117	            if path == "/v1/schedules":
118	                return self._create_schedule(self._body())
119	            schedule_dispatch = re.fullmatch(r"/v1/schedules/([^/]+)/dispatch", path)
120	            if schedule_dispatch:
121	                return self._dispatch_schedule(unquote(schedule_dispatch.group(1)), self._body())
122	            action = re.fullmatch(r"/v1/runs/([^/]+)/(claim|complete|fail|decision|heartbeat)", path)
123	            if action:
124	                if action.group(2) == "decision":
125	                    return self._decision(action.group(1), self._body())
126	                if action.group(2) == "heartbeat":
127	                    return self._heartbeat(action.group(1), self._body())
128	                return self._step_action(action.group(1), action.group(2), self._body())
129	        solo = re.fullmatch(r"/v1/runs/([^/]+)", path)
130	        if method == "GET" and solo:
131	            return self._get_run(query, solo.group(1))
132	        return self._error(404, "no route for %s %s" % (method, path))
133	
134	    # -- handlers ------------------------------------------------------
135	    def _get_run(self, query, run_id):
136	        tenant = self._tenant(query)
137	        owner = self.scheduler.store.run_exists(run_id)
138	        if owner is not None and owner != tenant:
139	            raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
140	        return self._json(200, _run_view(self.scheduler.get_run(tenant, run_id)))
141	
142	    def _list_runs(self, query):
143	        tenant = self._tenant(query)
144	        items, next_after = self.scheduler.list_runs(
145	            tenant,
146	            status=(query.get("status") or [None])[0],
147	            limit=int((query.get("limit") or ["50"])[0]),
148	            after=(query.get("after") or [None])[0],
149	        )
150	        return self._json(200, {"tenant": tenant, "items": [_run_view(r) for r in items],
151	                                "next_after": next_after})
152	
153	    # -- audit stream ----------------------------------------------------
154	    @staticmethod
155	    def _query_int(query, name, default, code):
156	        raw = (query.get(name) or [None])[0]
157	        if raw is None:
158	            return default
159	        try:
160	            return int(raw, 10)
161	        except ValueError:
162	            raise WorkflowError("%s must be an integer" % name, code)
163	
164	    def _list_audit(self, query):
165	        tenant = (query.get("tenant") or [None])[0]
166	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant.strip():
167	            raise WorkflowError("tenant must be a non-empty string", "bad_tenant")
168	        limit = self._query_int(query, "limit", 100, "bad_limit")
169	        if not 1 <= limit <= 1000:
170	            raise WorkflowError("limit must be an integer between 1 and 1000", "bad_limit")
171	        after = self._query_int(query, "after", 0, "bad_after")
172	        if after < 0:
173	            raise WorkflowError("after must be a non-negative integer", "bad_after")
174	        action = (query.get("action") or [None])[0]
175	        if action is not None and not action.strip():
176	            raise WorkflowError("action must be a non-empty string", "bad_action")
177	        run_id = (query.get("run_id") or [None])[0]
178	        if run_id is not None and not run_id.strip():
179	            raise WorkflowError("run_id must be a non-empty string", "bad_run_id")
180	        items, next_after = self.scheduler.list_audit(
181	            tenant, action=action, run_id=run_id, limit=limit, after=after)
182	        return self._json(200, {"tenant": tenant.strip(), "items": items,
183	                                "next_after": next_after})
184	
185	    # -- periodic schedules -------------------------------------------
186	    def _create_schedule(self, body):
187	        record = self.scheduler.create_schedule(
188	            self._tenant({}, body), body.get("schedule_id"), body.get("workflow_id"),
189	            body.get("interval_seconds"), body.get("first_at"), body.get("params"),
190	            body.get("max_parallelism"),
191	        )
192	        return self._json(201, _schedule_view(record))
193	
194	    def _list_schedules(self, query):
195	        tenant = self._tenant(query)
196	        return self._json(200, {"tenant": tenant,
197	                                "items": [_schedule_view(r)
198	                                          for r in self.scheduler.list_schedules(tenant)]})
199	
200	    def _dispatch_schedule(self, schedule_id, body):
201	        run, scheduled_at = self.scheduler.dispatch_schedule(self._tenant({}, body),
202	                                                              schedule_id)
203	        if run is None:
204	            return self._send(204)
205	        return self._json(201, _run_view(run, scheduled_at=scheduled_at))
206	
207	    # -- worker registry -----------------------------------------------
208	    def _worker_lease(self, body):
209	        """Extract lease_seconds: omitted defaults to 30, explicit null is 400."""
210	        if "lease_seconds" not in body:
211	            return 30
212	        lease = body["lease_seconds"]
213	        if lease is None:
214	            raise WorkflowError("lease_seconds must be a positive number", "bad_lease")
215	        return lease
216	
217	    def _register_worker(self, body):
218	        record, created = self.scheduler.register_worker(
219	            body.get("tenant"), body.get("worker_id"), self._worker_lease(body)
220	        )
221	        return self._json(201 if created else 200, record)
222	
223	    def _worker_heartbeat(self, worker_id, body):
224	        record = self.scheduler.heartbeat_worker(
225	            body.get("tenant"), worker_id, self._worker_lease(body)
226	        )
227	        return self._json(200, record)
228	
229	    def _list_workers(self, query):
230	        tenant = self._tenant(query)
231	        return self._json(200, {"tenant": tenant,
232	                                "items": self.scheduler.list_workers(tenant)})
233	
234	    def _claim_any_task(self, body):
235	        """Tenant-wide fair claim: 200 {"run_id","step"} or 204 when idle."""
236	        lease = body.get("lease_seconds", 30)
237	        if lease is None:
238	            raise WorkflowError("lease_seconds must be a positive number", "bad_lease")
239	        result = self.scheduler.claim_fair(body.get("tenant"), body.get("worker_id"), lease)
240	        if result is None:
241	            return self._send(204)
242	        run_id, step = result
243	        return self._json(200, {"run_id": run_id, "step": _step_view(step)})
244	
245	    def _step_action(self, run_id, action, body):
246	        tenant, worker_id = self._tenant({}, body), body.get("worker_id")
247	        if action == "claim":
248	            step = self.scheduler.claim(tenant, run_id, worker_id, body.get("lease_seconds", 30))
249	            return self._send(204) if step is None else self._json(200, {"step": _step_view(step)})
250	        if action == "complete":
251	            run = self.scheduler.complete(tenant, run_id, body.get("step_id"), worker_id,
252	                                          body.get("result"))
253	        else:
254	            run = self.scheduler.fail(tenant, run_id, body.get("step_id"), worker_id,
255	                                      body.get("error"))
256	        return self._json(200, _run_view(run))
257	
258	    def _heartbeat(self, run_id, body):
259	        """Renew a lease; strict field validation, anything bad is a 400."""
260	        for name in ("tenant", "step_id", "worker_id"):
261	            value = body.get(name)
262	            if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
263	                raise WorkflowError("%s must be a non-empty string" % name, "bad_%s" % name)
264	        run = self.scheduler.heartbeat(body["tenant"], run_id, body["step_id"],
265	                                       body["worker_id"], body.get("lease_seconds", 30))
266	        return self._json(200, _run_view(run))
267	
268	    def _decision(self, run_id, body):
269	        """Validate strictly; any missing/blank/wrong-type field is a 400."""
270	        fields = {}
271	        for name in ("tenant", "step_id", "actor"):
272	            value = body.get(name)
273	            if not isinstance(value, str) or not value.strip():
274	                raise WorkflowError("%s must be a non-empty string" % name, "bad_%s" % name)
275	            fields[name] = value.strip()
276	        decision = body.get("decision")
277	        if decision not in DECISIONS:
278	            raise WorkflowError("decision must be one of %s" % ", ".join(DECISIONS),
279	                                "bad_decision")
280	        tenant = fields["tenant"]
281	        owner = self.scheduler.store.run_exists(run_id)
282	        if owner is not None and owner != tenant:
283	            raise WorkflowError("run %s belongs to another tenant" % run_id, "cross_tenant")
284	        run = self.scheduler.decide(tenant, run_id, fields["step_id"], fields["actor"], decision)
285	        return self._json(200, _run_view(run))
286

290	            "attempt": step["attempt"],
291	            "max_attempts": step["max_attempts"], "depends_on": list(step["depends_on"]),
292	            "worker_id": step["worker_id"], "lease_deadline": step["lease_deadline"],
293	            "next_attempt_at": step["next_attempt_at"], "result": step.get("result"),

1	"""Persistence for flowd: workflows, runs, tenants and append-only history.
2	
3	Layout::
4	
5	    <root>/<tenant>/workflows.json
6	    <root>/<tenant>/idempotency.json
7	    <root>/<tenant>/workers.json
8	    <root>/<tenant>/schedules.json
9	    <root>/<tenant>/audit.json
10	    <root>/<tenant>/runs/<run_id>.json
11	
12	Every write is atomic (temp file + ``os.replace``) so a crash cannot leave a
13	half written run behind, and a fresh store over the same root sees exactly
14	the same workflows and runs.
15	"""
16	
17	import json
18	import os
19	import threading
20	import time as _time
21	import uuid
22	from contextlib import contextmanager
23	
24	from .model import KIND_TASK, WorkflowError, format_time, plan_workflow
25	
26	RUN_PENDING = "pending"
27	RUN_RUNNING = "running"
28	RUN_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
29	RUN_FAILED = "failed"
30	
31	STEP_PENDING = "pending"
32	STEP_READY = "ready"
33	STEP_RUNNING = "running"
34	STEP_WAITING = "waiting"
35	STEP_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
36	STEP_FAILED = "failed"
37	
38	TERMINAL_RUN_STATES = (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED)

41	def atomic_write_json(path, payload):
42	    """Write ``payload`` as JSON to ``path`` atomically."""
43	    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
44	    if directory:
45	        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
46	    tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
47	    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
48	        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
49	        handle.flush()
50	        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
51	    os.replace(tmp, path)
52	
53	
54	def read_json(path, default=None):
55	    try:
56	        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
57	            return json.load(handle)
58	    except FileNotFoundError:
59	        return default

62	class WorkflowStore:
63	    """Filesystem backed store for one data directory (all tenants)."""
64	
65	    def __init__(self, root, clock=None):
66	        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
67	        self._clock = clock if clock is not None else _time.time
68	        self._lock = threading.RLock()
69	        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)
70	
71	    def now(self):
72	        return float(self._clock())
73	
74	    def now_iso(self):
75	        return format_time(self.now())
76	
77	    @contextmanager
78	    def locked(self):
79	        with self._lock:
80	            yield
81	
82	    # -- paths ---------------------------------------------------------
83	    def tenant_dir(self, tenant):
84	        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant.strip():
85	            raise WorkflowError("tenant must be a non-empty string", "bad_tenant")
86	        return os.path.join(self.root, tenant.strip())
87	
88	    def workflows_path(self, tenant):
89	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workflows.json")
90	
91	    def idempotency_path(self, tenant):
92	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "idempotency.json")
93	
94	    def workers_path(self, tenant):
95	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workers.json")
96	
97	    def schedules_path(self, tenant):
98	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "schedules.json")
99	
100	    def audit_path(self, tenant):
101	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "audit.json")
102	
103	    def run_path(self, tenant, run_id):
104	        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)
105	
106	    def generate_run_id(self):
107	        return "run-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]
108	
109	    # -- workflows -----------------------------------------------------
110	    def save_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id, steps):
111	        plan = plan_workflow(workflow_id, steps)
112	        with self._lock:
113	            data = self.load_workflows(tenant)
114	            data[plan["workflow_id"]] = plan
115	            atomic_write_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), data)
116	        return plan
117	
118	    def load_workflows(self, tenant):
119	        return read_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), {}) or {}
120	
121	    def get_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id):
122	        plan = self.load_workflows(tenant).get(workflow_id)
123	        if plan is None:
124	            raise WorkflowError("unknown workflow: %s" % workflow_id, "unknown_workflow")
125	        return plan
126	
127	    # -- idempotency index --------------------------------------------
128	    def load_idempotency(self, tenant):
129	        """Return the tenant's ``{trimmed key: {"run_id": ...}}`` map."""
130	        return read_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), {}) or {}
131	
132	    def save_idempotency(self, tenant, index):
133	        atomic_write_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), index)
134	        return index
135	
136	    # -- worker registry ----------------------------------------------
137	    def load_workers(self, tenant):
138	        """Return the tenant's ``{worker_id: registration record}`` map."""
139	        return read_json(self.workers_path(tenant), {}) or {}
140	
141	    def save_workers(self, tenant, index):
142	        atomic_write_json(self.workers_path(tenant), index)
143	        return index
144	
145	    # -- schedule registry --------------------------------------------
146	    def load_schedules(self, tenant):
147	        """Return the tenant's ``{schedule_id: schedule record}`` map."""
148	        return read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}
149	
150	    def save_schedules(self, tenant, index):
151	        atomic_write_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), index)
152	        return index
153	
154	    def schedule_exists(self, schedule_id):
155	        """Return the tenant owning ``schedule_id``, or ``None``."""
156	        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
157	            if schedule_id in (read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}):
158	                return tenant
159	        return None
160	
161	    # -- audit stream ---------------------------------------------------
162	    def append_audit(self, tenant, action, at=None, run_id=None, step_id=None,
163	                     workflow_id=None, schedule_id=None, worker_id=None, actor=None):
164	        """Append one record to the tenant's audit stream.
165	
166	        The ``sequence`` is assigned under the store lock, so concurrent
167	        appends stay unique and follow commit order, and it continues from
168	        the persisted stream, so a restart keeps increasing.  Only
169	        identifiers and the actor are stored — never params, results or
170	        error text; identifiers that do not apply are ``None``.
171	        """
172	        with self._lock:
173	            path = self.audit_path(tenant)
174	            items = (read_json(path, None) or {}).get("items") or []
175	            record = {
176	                "sequence": (items[-1]["sequence"] + 1) if items else 1,
177	                "at": at if at is not None else self.now_iso(),
178	                "tenant": tenant.strip(),
179	                "action": action,
180	                "run_id": run_id,
181	                "step_id": step_id,
182	                "workflow_id": workflow_id,
183	                "schedule_id": schedule_id,
184	                "worker_id": worker_id,
185	                "actor": actor,
186	            }
187	            items.append(record)
188	            atomic_write_json(path, {"items": items})
189	            return dict(record)
190	
191	    def load_audit(self, tenant):
192	        """Return the tenant's audit records in sequence order (read-only)."""
193	        return list((read_json(self.audit_path(tenant), None) or {}).get("items") or [])
194	
195	    # -- runs ----------------------------------------------------------
196	    def save_run(self, run):
197	        atomic_write_json(self.run_path(run["tenant"], run["run_id"]), run)
198	        return run
199	
200	    def load_run(self, tenant, run_id):
201	        run = read_json(self.run_path(tenant, run_id), None)
202	        if run is None:
203	            raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
204	        return normalize_run(run)
205	
206	    def run_exists(self, run_id):
207	        """Return the tenant owning ``run_id``, or ``None``."""
208	        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
209	            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, tenant, "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)):
210	                return tenant
211	        return None
212	
213	    def load_all_runs(self, tenant):
214	        """Return every run of the tenant as a list sorted by ``run_id``."""
215	        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
216	        items = []
217	        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
218	            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
219	            if run is not None:
220	                items.append(normalize_run(run))
221	        items.sort(key=lambda r: r.get("run_id", ""))
222	        return items
223	
224	    def list_runs(self, tenant, status=None, limit=50, after=None):
225	        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
226	        items = []
227	        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
228	            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
229	            if run is not None:
230	                items.append(normalize_run(run))
231	        items.sort(key=lambda r: (r.get("created_at", ""), r.get("run_id", "")))
232	        if status:
233	            items = [r for r in items if r.get("status") == status]
234	        if after:
235	            position = [i for i, r in enumerate(items) if r.get("run_id") == after]
236	            items = items[position[0] + 1:] if position else []
237	        limit = max(1, int(limit))
238	        page = items[:limit]
239	        return page, (page[-1]["run_id"] if len(items) > limit else None)

242	def normalize_run(run):
243	    """Backfill fields missing from documents written by older versions.
244	
245	    Steps without ``kind`` predate approval nodes and are ordinary tasks.
246	    Runs without ``max_parallelism`` predate per-run concurrency quotas and
247	    have no limit (``None``).  Runs without ``idempotency_key`` predate
248	    tenant-scoped idempotency keys and never participate in dedup (``None``).
249	    Runs without ``not_before`` predate delayed start and begin immediately
250	    (``None``).  Runs without ``schedule_id``/``scheduled_at`` predate
251	    periodic scheduling and were created manually (``None``).  Steps without
252	    ``next_attempt_at`` predate retry backoff and are immediately claimable
253	    (``None``).  Runs without a frozen ``plan`` predate per-run DAG snapshots
254	    and reconstruct theirs from the node definitions and ``step_order`` saved
255	    in the run document itself, so replay never has to read the workflow
256	    registry (which a later same-name submission may have overwritten).
257	    Mutates and returns ``run``.
258	    """
259	    run.setdefault("max_parallelism", None)
260	    run.setdefault("idempotency_key", None)
261	    run.setdefault("not_before", None)
262	    run.setdefault("schedule_id", None)
263	    run.setdefault("scheduled_at", None)
264	    for step in run.get("steps", {}).values():
265	        step.setdefault("kind", KIND_TASK)
266	        step.setdefault("approval", None)
267	        step.setdefault("next_attempt_at", None)
268	    if not run.get("plan"):
269	        run["plan"] = plan_from_run(run)
270	    return run
271	
272	
273	def plan_from_run(run):
274	    """Reconstruct a normalized plan from the definitions frozen in a run.
275	
276	    The run document keeps each node's ``kind``, ``depends_on`` and
277	    ``max_attempts`` together with ``step_order``; those are exactly the
278	    fields a plan needs, so documents written before plans were snapshotted
279	    remain replayable even after the workflow of the same id is overwritten
280	    or deleted.
281	    """
282	    steps = run.get("steps") or {}
283	    order = [sid for sid in (run.get("step_order") or sorted(steps)) if sid in steps]
284	    ordered = [
285	        {

"""Persistence for flowd: workflows, runs, tenants and append-only history.

Layout::

    <root>/<tenant>/workflows.json
    <root>/<tenant>/idempotency.json
    <root>/<tenant>/workers.json
    <root>/<tenant>/schedules.json
    <root>/<tenant>/audit.json
    <root>/<tenant>/runs/<run_id>.json

Every write is atomic (temp file + ``os.replace``) so a crash cannot leave a
half written run behind, and a fresh store over the same root sees exactly
the same workflows and runs.
"""

import json
import os
import threading
import time as _time
import uuid
from contextlib import contextmanager

from .model import KIND_TASK, WorkflowError, format_time, plan_workflow

RUN_PENDING = "pending"
RUN_RUNNING = "running"
RUN_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
RUN_FAILED = "failed"

STEP_PENDING = "pending"
STEP_READY = "ready"
STEP_RUNNING = "running"
STEP_WAITING = "waiting"
STEP_SUCCEEDED = "succeeded"
STEP_FAILED = "failed"

TERMINAL_RUN_STATES = (RUN_SUCCEEDED, RUN_FAILED)


def atomic_write_json(path, payload):
    """Write ``payload`` as JSON to ``path`` atomically."""
    directory = os.path.dirname(path)
    if directory:
        os.makedirs(directory, exist_ok=True)
    tmp = "%s.tmp.%d" % (path, os.getpid())
    with open(tmp, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
        json.dump(payload, handle, ensure_ascii=True, sort_keys=True, indent=2)
        handle.flush()
        os.fsync(handle.fileno())
    os.replace(tmp, path)


def read_json(path, default=None):
    try:
        with open(path, "r", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
            return json.load(handle)
    except FileNotFoundError:
        return default


class WorkflowStore:
    """Filesystem backed store for one data directory (all tenants)."""

    def __init__(self, root, clock=None):
        self.root = os.path.abspath(root)
        self._clock = clock if clock is not None else _time.time
        self._lock = threading.RLock()
        os.makedirs(self.root, exist_ok=True)

    def now(self):
        return float(self._clock())

    def now_iso(self):
        return format_time(self.now())

    @contextmanager
    def locked(self):
        with self._lock:
            yield

    # -- paths ---------------------------------------------------------
    def tenant_dir(self, tenant):
        if not isinstance(tenant, str) or not tenant.strip():
            raise WorkflowError("tenant must be a non-empty string", "bad_tenant")
        return os.path.join(self.root, tenant.strip())

    def workflows_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workflows.json")

    def idempotency_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "idempotency.json")

    def workers_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "workers.json")

    def schedules_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "schedules.json")

    def audit_path(self, tenant):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "audit.json")

    def run_path(self, tenant, run_id):
        return os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)

    def generate_run_id(self):
        return "run-" + uuid.uuid4().hex[:12]

    # -- workflows -----------------------------------------------------
    def save_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id, steps):
        plan = plan_workflow(workflow_id, steps)
        with self._lock:
            data = self.load_workflows(tenant)
            data[plan["workflow_id"]] = plan
            atomic_write_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), data)
        return plan

    def load_workflows(self, tenant):
        return read_json(self.workflows_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def get_workflow(self, tenant, workflow_id):
        plan = self.load_workflows(tenant).get(workflow_id)
        if plan is None:
            raise WorkflowError("unknown workflow: %s" % workflow_id, "unknown_workflow")
        return plan

    # -- idempotency index --------------------------------------------
    def load_idempotency(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{trimmed key: {"run_id": ...}}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_idempotency(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.idempotency_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    # -- worker registry ----------------------------------------------
    def load_workers(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{worker_id: registration record}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.workers_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_workers(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.workers_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    # -- schedule registry --------------------------------------------
    def load_schedules(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's ``{schedule_id: schedule record}`` map."""
        return read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}

    def save_schedules(self, tenant, index):
        atomic_write_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), index)
        return index

    def schedule_exists(self, schedule_id):
        """Return the tenant owning ``schedule_id``, or ``None``."""
        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
            if schedule_id in (read_json(self.schedules_path(tenant), {}) or {}):
                return tenant
        return None

    # -- audit stream ---------------------------------------------------
    def append_audit(self, tenant, action, at=None, run_id=None, step_id=None,
                     workflow_id=None, schedule_id=None, worker_id=None, actor=None):
        """Append one record to the tenant's audit stream.

        The ``sequence`` is assigned under the store lock, so concurrent
        appends stay unique and follow commit order, and it continues from
        the persisted stream, so a restart keeps increasing.  Only
        identifiers and the actor are stored — never params, results or
        error text; identifiers that do not apply are ``None``.
        """
        with self._lock:
            path = self.audit_path(tenant)
            items = (read_json(path, None) or {}).get("items") or []
            record = {
                "sequence": (items[-1]["sequence"] + 1) if items else 1,
                "at": at if at is not None else self.now_iso(),
                "tenant": tenant.strip(),
                "action": action,
                "run_id": run_id,
                "step_id": step_id,
                "workflow_id": workflow_id,
                "schedule_id": schedule_id,
                "worker_id": worker_id,
                "actor": actor,
            }
            items.append(record)
            atomic_write_json(path, {"items": items})
            return dict(record)

    def load_audit(self, tenant):
        """Return the tenant's audit records in sequence order (read-only)."""
        return list((read_json(self.audit_path(tenant), None) or {}).get("items") or [])

    # -- runs ----------------------------------------------------------
    def save_run(self, run):
        atomic_write_json(self.run_path(run["tenant"], run["run_id"]), run)
        return run

    def load_run(self, tenant, run_id):
        run = read_json(self.run_path(tenant, run_id), None)
        if run is None:
            raise WorkflowError("unknown run: %s" % run_id, "unknown_run")
        return normalize_run(run)

    def run_exists(self, run_id):
        """Return the tenant owning ``run_id``, or ``None``."""
        for tenant in sorted(os.listdir(self.root)):
            if os.path.isfile(os.path.join(self.root, tenant, "runs", "%s.json" % run_id)):
                return tenant
        return None

    def load_all_runs(self, tenant):
        """Return every run of the tenant as a list sorted by ``run_id``."""
        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
        items = []
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
            if run is not None:
                items.append(normalize_run(run))
        items.sort(key=lambda r: r.get("run_id", ""))
        return items

    def list_runs(self, tenant, status=None, limit=50, after=None):
        runs_dir = os.path.join(self.tenant_dir(tenant), "runs")
        items = []
        for name in sorted(os.listdir(runs_dir)) if os.path.isdir(runs_dir) else []:
            run = read_json(os.path.join(runs_dir, name), None) if name.endswith(".json") else None
            if run is not None:
                items.append(normalize_run(run))
        items.sort(key=lambda r: (r.get("created_at", ""), r.get("run_id", "")))
        if status:
            items = [r for r in items if r.get("status") == status]
        if after:
            position = [i for i, r in enumerate(items) if r.get("run_id") == after]
            items = items[position[0] + 1:] if position else []
        limit = max(1, int(limit))
        page = items[:limit]
        return page, (page[-1]["run_id"] if len(items) > limit else None)


def normalize_run(run):
    """Backfill fields missing from documents written by older versions.

    Steps without ``kind`` predate approval nodes and are ordinary tasks.
    Runs without ``max_parallelism`` predate per-run concurrency quotas and
    have no limit (``None``).  Runs without ``idempotency_key`` predate
    tenant-scoped idempotency keys and never participate in dedup (``None``).
    Runs without ``not_before`` predate delayed start and begin immediately
    (``None``).  Runs without ``schedule_id``/``scheduled_at`` predate
    periodic scheduling and were created manually (``None``).  Steps without
    ``next_attempt_at`` predate retry backoff and are immediately claimable
    (``None``).  Runs without a frozen ``plan`` predate per-run DAG snapshots
    and reconstruct theirs from the node definitions and ``step_order`` saved
    in the run document itself, so replay never has to read the workflow
    registry (which a later same-name submission may have overwritten).
    Mutates and returns ``run``.
    """
    run.setdefault("max_parallelism", None)
    run.setdefault("idempotency_key", None)
    run.setdefault("not_before", None)
    run.setdefault("schedule_id", None)
    run.setdefault("scheduled_at", None)
    for step in run.get("steps", {}).values():
        step.setdefault("kind", KIND_TASK)
        step.setdefault("approval", None)
        step.setdefault("next_attempt_at", None)
    if not run.get("plan"):
        run["plan"] = plan_from_run(run)
    return run


def plan_from_run(run):
    """Reconstruct a normalized plan from the definitions frozen in a run.

    The run document keeps each node's ``kind``, ``depends_on`` and
    ``max_attempts`` together with ``step_order``; those are exactly the
    fields a plan needs, so documents written before plans were snapshotted
    remain replayable even after the workflow of the same id is overwritten
    or deleted.
    """
    steps = run.get("steps") or {}
    order = [sid for sid in (run.get("step_order") or sorted(steps)) if sid in steps]
    ordered = [
        {
            "id": steps[sid]["id"],
            "depends_on": list(steps[sid].get("depends_on") or []),
            "max_attempts": steps[sid]["max_attempts"],
            "kind": steps[sid].get("kind", KIND_TASK),
        }
        for sid in order
    ]
    return {
        "workflow_id": run.get("workflow_id"),
        "steps": ordered,
        "order": [step["id"] for step in ordered],
    }


def run_plan(run):
    """Return the normalized DAG plan frozen into ``run`` at creation.

    Newer documents carry an explicit snapshot under ``plan``; older ones
    reconstruct it via :func:`plan_from_run` from the run's own nodes and
    ordering.  The result is a fresh copy, so callers can never mutate the
    snapshot stored in the run document.
    """
    snapshot = run.get("plan")
    if not snapshot or not snapshot.get("steps"):
        snapshot = plan_from_run(run)
    return {
        "workflow_id": snapshot.get("workflow_id", run.get("workflow_id")),
        "steps": [dict(step) for step in snapshot.get("steps", [])],
        "order": list(snapshot.get("order", [])),
    }


def new_run(tenant, workflow_id, run_id, params, plan, now_iso, max_parallelism=None,
            idempotency_key=None, not_before=None, schedule_id=None, scheduled_at=None):
    """Build a fresh run document from a validated plan."""
    steps = {
        step["id"]: {
            "id": step["id"],
            "kind": step.get("kind", KIND_TASK),
            "depends_on": list(step["depends_on"]),
            "max_attempts": step["max_attempts"],
            "status": STEP_PENDING,
            "attempt": 0,
            "worker_id": None,
            "lease_deadline": None,
            "next_attempt_at": None,
            "ready_at": None,
            "started_at": None,
            "finished_at": None,
            "result": None,
            "error": None,
            "approval": None,
        }
        for step in plan["steps"]
    }
    return {
        "tenant": tenant,
        "workflow_id": workflow_id,
        "run_id": run_id,
        "status": RUN_PENDING,
        "params": params or {},
        "max_parallelism": max_parallelism,
        "idempotency_key": idempotency_key,
        "not_before": not_before,
        "schedule_id": schedule_id,
        "scheduled_at": scheduled_at,
        "created_at": now_iso,
        "updated_at": now_iso,
        # The normalized DAG as it was when this run was created.  A later
        # submission of another workflow with the same id must not rewrite
        # this run's nodes, order, kinds, dependencies or max_attempts;
        # replay rebuilds exclusively from this snapshot.
        "plan": {
            "workflow_id": plan["workflow_id"],
            "steps": [dict(step) for step in plan["steps"]],
            "order": list(plan["order"]),
        },
        "step_order": list(plan["order"]),
        "order_index": {sid: i for i, sid in enumerate(plan["order"])},
        "steps": steps,
        "history": [],
    }

# flowd

A minimal but real **distributed task scheduling / workflow orchestration backend**:
DAG definition and validation, run state machine, worker leases with expiry and
takeover, retries with exponential backoff, idempotent completion, human
**approval nodes**, append-only history with replay, multi-tenant isolation, and
a small JSON HTTP API. Standard library only: no pip installs, no network
access, no third-party imports.

Data lives in a single directory: `<root>/<tenant>/workflows.json`,
`<root>/<tenant>/idempotency.json` (idempotency-key → run bindings),
`<root>/<tenant>/workers.json` (worker registrations),
`<root>/<tenant>/schedules.json` (periodic schedules),
`<root>/<tenant>/audit.json` (the tenant's audit stream) plus
`<root>/<tenant>/runs/<run_id>.json`, written atomically, so restarting the
process sees exactly the same state.

## Run

```bash
# HTTP API (default data dir ./flowd_data)
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data serve --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8080

# tests
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v
```

## CLI

Global `--data-dir` goes **before** the subcommand. Every command prints one line
of JSON on stdout; errors print one line of JSON on stderr and exit non-zero.

```bash
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data submit --tenant acme --workflow etl --file steps.json
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data status --run-id run-abc --tenant acme
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data claim --run-id run-abc --tenant acme --worker w1
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data complete --run-id run-abc --step step1 --tenant acme --worker w1
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data fail --run-id run-abc --step step1 --tenant acme --worker w1 --error boom
python3 -m flowd --data-dir ./flowd_data list --tenant acme
```

`steps.json` is a JSON list of steps, e.g.
`[{"id": "step1", "depends_on": []}, {"id": "step2", "depends_on": ["step1"], "max_attempts": 3}]`.
A step may set `"kind": "approval"` (default `"task"`) to insert a human gate;
the only accepted values are `task` and `approval`.

## HTTP API

| Method | Path | Success | Error codes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| GET | `/healthz` | 200 `{"ok":true}` | - |
| POST | `/v1/workflows` | 201 validated plan | 400 validation error, 400 bad JSON |
| POST | `/v1/runs` | 201 run (new or replayed) | 400 bad request/max_parallelism/idempotency_key/params/not_before, 404 unknown workflow, 409 idempotency conflict |
| GET | `/v1/runs/{run_id}?tenant=` | 200 run with step states | 400 missing tenant, 403 cross-tenant, 404 unknown run |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/claim` | 200 `{"step":...}`, 204 nothing ready | 400 bad request, 403 cross-tenant, 404 unknown run, 409 worker not registered/expired |
| POST | `/v1/tasks/claim` | 200 `{"run_id":...,"step":...}`, 204 nothing claimable | 400 bad tenant/worker_id/lease_seconds/JSON, 409 worker not registered/expired |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/complete` | 200 updated run | 400 bad request, 403, 404 unknown step, 409 lease not held/expired |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/fail` | 200 updated run | 400 bad request, 403, 404 unknown step, 409 lease not held/expired |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/decision` | 200 updated run | 400 bad request/JSON, 403 cross-tenant, 404 unknown run/step, 409 not an approval/not waiting/already decided |
| POST | `/v1/runs/{run_id}/heartbeat` | 200 updated run | 400 bad request/JSON, 403 cross-tenant, 404 unknown run/step, 409 finished run/approval node/lease not held/expired |
| POST | `/v1/workers/register` | 201 new registration, 200 refreshed registration | 400 bad tenant/worker_id/lease_seconds/JSON |
| POST | `/v1/workers/{worker_id}/heartbeat` | 200 registration record | 400 bad tenant/lease_seconds/JSON, 404 unknown worker, 409 worker_expired |
| GET | `/v1/workers?tenant=` | 200 `{"tenant":...,"items":[...]}` sorted by worker_id | 400 missing tenant |
| POST | `/v1/schedules` | 201 schedule record with `next_at` | 400 bad_tenant/bad_schedule_id/bad_interval/bad_first_at/bad_params/bad_max_parallelism/bad JSON, 404 unknown workflow, 409 schedule_exists |
| GET | `/v1/schedules?tenant=` | 200 `{"tenant":...,"items":[...]}` sorted by schedule_id | 400 missing tenant |
| POST | `/v1/schedules/{schedule_id}/dispatch` | 201 scheduled run, 204 not due yet | 400 bad_tenant/bad_schedule_id/bad JSON, 403 cross-tenant, 404 unknown schedule |
| GET | `/v1/runs?tenant=&status=&limit=&after=` | 200 `{"items":[...],"next_after":...}` | 400 missing tenant |
| GET | `/v1/audit?tenant=&action=&run_id=&limit=&after=` | 200 `{"tenant":...,"items":[...],"next_after":...}` | 400 bad_tenant/bad_action/bad_run_id/bad_limit/bad_after |

Errors are always `{"error": "<message>"}`.

### Tenant-scoped audit stream

Every state change also appends one record to the tenant's audit stream,
stored in `<tenant>/audit.json` and readable via
`GET /v1/audit?tenant=` (or `Scheduler.list_audit`). Each record is

```json
{"sequence": 7, "at": "2026-01-01T00:00:00.000000Z", "tenant": "acme",
 "action": "claim", "run_id": "r1", "step_id": "step1",
 "workflow_id": "etl", "schedule_id": null, "worker_id": "w1", "actor": null}
```

Run actions reuse the existing history types (`run_created`, `ready`,
`waiting`, `claim`, `heartbeat`, `takeover`, `complete`, `fail`, `retry`,
`attempts_exhausted`, `decision`, `run_started`, `run_succeeded`,
`run_failed`); control-plane operations use fixed `resource.action`
identifiers: `workflow.submit`, `worker.register`, `worker.heartbeat`,
`schedule.create` and `schedule.dispatch`. Records carry only identifiers
and the actor (the decision maker on `decision` records, `null` elsewhere)
— never params, results or error text; identifiers that do not apply are
`null`. When one request causes several changes (e.g. two lease takeovers
plus a claim), the records enter the stream in the order the changes
actually happened.

`sequence` starts at 1 per tenant and is assigned under the store lock in
commit order, so it is gap-free, unique under concurrency and keeps
increasing across restarts. Query parameters: `tenant` is required and
must be a non-empty string (`bad_tenant`); `limit` defaults to 100 and
accepts only integers from 1 to 1000 (`bad_limit`); `after` defaults to 0

        ``cancel`` event carrying the previous lease holder and the actor,

        A sleeping run (a future ``not_before``) is cancelled without
        opening its root nodes.  Nothing is deleted: the run file, the

"""Tests for run-level cancellation: state machine, history, audit, replay."""

import shutil
import tempfile
import unittest

from flowd.model import WorkflowError
from flowd.scheduler import ConflictError, LeaseError, Scheduler
from flowd.store import WorkflowStore


class FakeClock:
    def __init__(self, start=1_700_000_000.0):
        self.value = float(start)

    def __call__(self):
        return self.value

    def advance(self, seconds):
        self.value += float(seconds)
        return self.value


LINEAR = [
    {"id": "step1", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "step2", "depends_on": ["step1"]},
    {"id": "step3", "depends_on": ["step2"]},
]


class CancelTestBase(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="flowd-cancel-")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        self.clock = FakeClock()
        self.store = WorkflowStore(self.root, clock=self.clock)
        self.scheduler = Scheduler(self.store, clock=self.clock)

    def start(self, steps=None, workflow_id="wf", run_id="r1", tenant="acme", **kw):
        self.scheduler.submit(tenant, workflow_id, LINEAR if steps is None else steps)
        return self.scheduler.start_run(tenant, workflow_id, run_id=run_id, **kw)

    def cancel(self, run_id="r1", tenant="acme", actor="ops"):
        return self.scheduler.cancel(tenant, run_id, actor)


class CancelValidationTest(CancelTestBase):
    def test_bad_tenant(self):
        self.start()
        for bad in (None, "", "   ", 3, True, ["acme"]):
            with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
                self.scheduler.cancel(bad, "r1", "ops")
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "bad_tenant", "value %r" % (bad,))

    def test_bad_actor(self):
        self.start()
        for bad in (None, "", "   ", 3, True, ["ops"]):
            with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
                self.scheduler.cancel("acme", "r1", bad)
            self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "bad_actor", "value %r" % (bad,))

    def test_tenant_and_actor_are_trimmed(self):
        self.start()
        run = self.scheduler.cancel("  acme  ", "r1", "  ops  ")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "cancelled")
        event = run["history"][-1]
        self.assertEqual(event["type"], "run_cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(event["actor"], "ops")

    def test_unknown_run(self):
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.cancel("acme", "ghost", "ops")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "unknown_run")

    def test_cross_tenant(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.submit("other", "wf", LINEAR)
        with self.assertRaises(WorkflowError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.cancel("other", "r1", "ops")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "cross_tenant")


class CancelLifecycleTest(CancelTestBase):
    def test_cancel_pending_run(self):
        self.start()
        run = self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "cancelled")
        for sid in ("step1", "step2", "step3"):
            step = run["steps"][sid]
            self.assertEqual(step["status"], "cancelled")
            self.assertIsNone(step["worker_id"])
            self.assertIsNone(step["lease_deadline"])
            self.assertIsNone(step["next_attempt_at"])
            self.assertEqual(step["attempt"], 0)
            self.assertIsNone(step["result"])
            self.assertIsNone(step["error"])
        types = [e["type"] for e in run["history"]]
        self.assertEqual(types, ["run_created", "ready", "cancel", "cancel",
                                 "cancel", "run_cancelled"])
        cancels = [e for e in run["history"] if e["type"] == "cancel"]
        self.assertEqual([e["step_id"] for e in cancels], ["step1", "step2", "step3"])
        for event in cancels:
            self.assertIsNone(event["worker_id"])
            self.assertEqual(event["actor"], "ops")
        last = run["history"][-1]
        self.assertIsNone(last["step_id"])
        self.assertEqual(last["actor"], "ops")

    def test_cancel_running_run_clears_lease_but_keeps_attempt(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1", lease_seconds=30)
        run = self.cancel(actor="admin")
        step = run["steps"]["step1"]
        self.assertEqual(step["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertIsNone(step["worker_id"])
        self.assertIsNone(step["lease_deadline"])
        self.assertIsNone(step["next_attempt_at"])
        cancel_event = [e for e in run["history"]
                        if e["type"] == "cancel" and e["step_id"] == "step1"][0]
        self.assertEqual(cancel_event["worker_id"], "w1")
        self.assertEqual(cancel_event["actor"], "admin")

    def test_cancel_keeps_succeeded_nodes_and_failure_state(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.scheduler.complete("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", result={"rows": 3})
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.scheduler.fail("acme", "r1", "step2", "w1", error="boom")
        run = self.cancel()
        step1 = run["steps"]["step1"]
        self.assertEqual(step1["status"], "succeeded")
        self.assertEqual(step1["result"], {"rows": 3})
        self.assertEqual(step1["worker_id"], "w1")
        step2 = run["steps"]["step2"]
        self.assertEqual(step2["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(step2["attempt"], 1)
        self.assertEqual(step2["error"], "boom")
        self.assertIsNone(step2["next_attempt_at"])
        # No cancel event for the already-succeeded node.
        cancelled = [e["step_id"] for e in run["history"] if e["type"] == "cancel"]
        self.assertEqual(cancelled, ["step2", "step3"])

    def test_cancel_waiting_approval_node(self):
        self.start([{"id": "gate", "depends_on": [], "kind": "approval"}])
        run = self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(run["steps"]["gate"]["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertIsNone(run["steps"]["gate"]["approval"])

    def test_cancel_sleeping_run_does_not_open_roots(self):
        self.start(not_before=self.clock.value + 3600)
        run = self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "cancelled")
        types = [e["type"] for e in run["history"]]
        self.assertNotIn("ready", types)
        self.assertNotIn("waiting", types)
        self.assertEqual(types, ["run_created", "cancel", "cancel", "cancel",
                                 "run_cancelled"])

    def test_repeat_cancel_is_a_noop(self):
        self.start()
        first = self.cancel()
        self.clock.advance(60)
        second = self.cancel(actor="someone-else")
        self.assertEqual(second["updated_at"], first["updated_at"])
        self.assertEqual(len(second["history"]), len(first["history"]))
        audit_before = self.store.load_audit("acme")
        self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(self.store.load_audit("acme"), audit_before)

    def test_finished_run_conflicts(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.scheduler.fail("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", error="x")
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.scheduler.fail("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", error="x")
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        run = self.scheduler.fail("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", error="x")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "failed")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_finished")

    def test_succeeded_run_conflicts(self):
        self.start([{"id": "only", "depends_on": []}])
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        run = self.scheduler.complete("acme", "r1", "only", "w1")
        self.assertEqual(run["status"], "succeeded")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_finished")

    def test_audit_stream_records_cancel_in_order(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.cancel(actor="admin")
        actions = [r["action"] for r in self.store.load_audit("acme")]
        self.assertEqual(actions[-5:], ["cancel", "cancel", "cancel",
                                        "run_cancelled", ] [:4] + ["run_cancelled"][:0]
                         or actions[-4:])
        tail = self.store.load_audit("acme")[-4:]
        self.assertEqual([r["action"] for r in tail],
                         ["cancel", "cancel", "cancel", "run_cancelled"])
        self.assertEqual([r["step_id"] for r in tail],
                         ["step1", "step2", "step3", None])
        self.assertTrue(all(r["actor"] == "admin" for r in tail))
        self.assertEqual([r["worker_id"] for r in tail], ["w1", None, None, None])


class CancelInteractionTest(CancelTestBase):
    def setUp(self):
        super().setUp()
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.cancel()

    def test_claim_returns_none_without_takeover(self):
        history_len = len(self.scheduler.get_run("acme", "r1")["history"])
        self.assertIsNone(self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w2"))
        run = self.scheduler.get_run("acme", "r1")
        self.assertEqual(len(run["history"]), history_len)
        self.assertNotIn("takeover", [e["type"] for e in run["history"]])

    def test_claim_fair_skips_cancelled_run(self):
        self.assertIsNone(self.scheduler.claim_fair("acme", "w2"))

    def test_complete_fail_heartbeat_decision_conflict(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.complete("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_cancelled")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.fail("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", error="x")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_cancelled")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.heartbeat("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_cancelled")

    def test_decision_on_cancelled_run_conflicts(self):
        self.start([{"id": "gate", "depends_on": [], "kind": "approval"}],
                   workflow_id="wf2", run_id="r2")
        self.cancel(run_id="r2")
        with self.assertRaises(ConflictError) as ctx:
            self.scheduler.decide("acme", "r2", "gate", "alice", "approve")
        self.assertEqual(ctx.exception.code, "run_cancelled")

    def test_list_and_get_show_cancelled(self):
        items, _ = self.scheduler.list_runs("acme", status="cancelled")
        self.assertEqual([r["run_id"] for r in items], ["r1"])
        items, _ = self.scheduler.list_runs("acme", status="running")
        self.assertEqual(items, [])

    def test_idempotency_binding_survives_cancel(self):
        self.scheduler.submit("acme", "wf3", LINEAR)
        self.scheduler.start_run("acme", "wf3", run_id="r3", idempotency_key="k1")
        self.scheduler.cancel("acme", "r3", "ops")
        replayed = self.scheduler.start_run("acme", "wf3", run_id="r3",
                                            idempotency_key="k1")
        self.assertEqual(replayed["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(replayed["run_id"], "r3")


class CancelReplayTest(CancelTestBase):
    def test_replay_rebuilds_cancelled_state(self):
        self.start()
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        self.scheduler.complete("acme", "r1", "step1", "w1", result=1)
        self.scheduler.claim("acme", "r1", "w1")
        stored = self.cancel(actor="admin")
        rebuilt = self.scheduler.replay("acme", "r1")
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt, stored)
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt["steps"]["step1"]["status"], "succeeded")
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt["steps"]["step2"]["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt["steps"]["step3"]["status"], "cancelled")

    def test_replay_after_restart(self):
        self.start(not_before=self.clock.value + 3600)
        stored = self.cancel()
        fresh = Scheduler(WorkflowStore(self.root, clock=self.clock), clock=self.clock)
        rebuilt = fresh.replay("acme", "r1")
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt, stored)
        self.assertEqual(rebuilt["status"], "cancelled")
        loaded = fresh.get_run("acme", "r1")
        self.assertEqual(loaded["updated_at"], stored["updated_at"])
        audit = [r["action"] for r in fresh.list_audit("acme")[0]]
        self.assertEqual(audit[-4:], ["cancel", "cancel", "cancel", "run_cancelled"])


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()

"""End-to-end tests for POST /v1/runs/{run_id}/cancel."""

import json
import shutil
import tempfile
import threading
import unittest
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

from flowd.http_app import create_server
from flowd.store import WorkflowStore

LINEAR = [
    {"id": "step1", "depends_on": []},
    {"id": "step2", "depends_on": ["step1"]},
]


class HttpCancelTest(unittest.TestCase):
    def setUp(self):
        self.root = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="flowd-http-cancel-")
        self.addCleanup(shutil.rmtree, self.root, True)
        self.server = create_server(WorkflowStore(self.root), "127.0.0.1", 0)
        self.port = self.server.server_address[1]
        threading.Thread(target=self.server.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        self.addCleanup(self.server.server_close)
        self.addCleanup(self.server.shutdown)

    def call(self, method, path, body=None, raw_body=None):
        """Return (status, parsed json or None); never raises on HTTP errors."""
        data = raw_body
        if body is not None:
            data = json.dumps(body).encode("utf-8")
        request = urllib.request.Request("http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (self.port, path),
                                        data=data, method=method)
        if data is not None:
            request.add_header("Content-Type", "application/json")
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen(request, timeout=10) as response:
                payload = response.read()
                return response.status, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)
        except urllib.error.HTTPError as exc:
            payload = exc.read()
            return exc.code, (json.loads(payload) if payload else None)

    def start_run(self, tenant="acme", run_id="r1"):
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/workflows",
                                 {"tenant": tenant, "workflow_id": "etl", "steps": LINEAR})
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs",
                                 {"tenant": tenant, "workflow_id": "etl", "run_id": run_id})
        self.assertEqual(status, 201, body)
        return body

    def cancel(self, run_id="r1", tenant="acme", actor="ops"):
        return self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/%s/cancel" % run_id,
                         {"tenant": tenant, "actor": actor})

    def test_cancel_returns_200_run_view(self):
        self.start_run()
        status, body = self.cancel()
        self.assertEqual(status, 200, body)
        self.assertEqual(body["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual([s["status"] for s in body["steps"]],
                         ["cancelled", "cancelled"])
        # The same state is visible through GET and list.
        status, fetched = self.call("GET", "/v1/runs/r1?tenant=acme")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(fetched["status"], "cancelled")
        self.assertEqual(fetched["updated_at"], body["updated_at"])
        status, listing = self.call("GET", "/v1/runs?tenant=acme&status=cancelled")
        self.assertEqual([r["run_id"] for r in listing["items"]], ["r1"])

    def test_repeat_cancel_returns_same_run_without_new_history(self):
        self.start_run()
        _, first = self.cancel()
        status, second = self.cancel(actor="other")
        self.assertEqual(status, 200)
        self.assertEqual(second["updated_at"], first["updated_at"])
        self.assertEqual(second["history_length"], first["history_length"])

    def test_bad_json(self):
        self.start_run()
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/r1/cancel", raw_body=b"{nope")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
        status, body = self.call("POST", "/v1/runs/r1/cancel", raw_body=b"[1, 2]")
        self.assertEqual(status, 400)
